Anyway, one thing I'd like to add is that there are a lot of options for leg exercises that rarely get mentioned. Doing weighted squats and deadlifts is great, very few people take offense to that suggestion even here. But for lower body stuff you should be doing more than one lower-body exercise in your routine. The single leg deadlift is very simple and a good supplemental exercise for beginners. Here's Al Kavadlowith it. The back bridge can also be a good leg exercise. Try to push with your heels.

After that you should look up falling towers, sissy squats, and nordic hamstring curls for better leg development, though all of these are fairly tough, but they should be added to your routine to help offset the criminal lack of lower-body work. Hill sprints are one of the best things to do as well, but they can be hard to fit in an existing routine. But the squat progression is nowhere near enough for leg development. And best of luck on your new routine!
